My own ruling 4 dropped the position-cache gitignore entry on the premise 'no gate produces a position cache'. The reviewer verified that premise is TRUE and showed the conclusion I drew from it was the wrong one of two available readings: the correct reading is that a human-confirmed deliverable lost its owning gate when the queue was cut to nine. Provenance is settled/human, so this is not mine to settle and not the reviewer's. Escalated to the human as a straight either/or: (a) assign the position cache and suffix removal to a named gate, or (b) amend the ruling to accept positions inside committed pages and record SY1's measured churn cost (~450 position-bearing lines rewritten per 3-line source edit) as accepted.

The rebuildable position store the ruling calls for therefore substantially EXISTS; option (a)'s remaining work is dropping the page suffix plus a test, not building a new cache. This materially lowers the cost of (a) and is stated to the human as such.
payload.b2: A check that cannot fail, in shipped code. render.py:397-419 increments npages once per write_text() CALL rather than once per distinct output path, so render_report.json's 'pages' field is identical in the healthy world and in a world where pages overwrite each other. Confirmed by me: render_report.json pages=3636, .md files on disk=3635, and this gate's own checks.py prints 'pages scanned: 3635' beside it. Two g0 artifacts disagree by one in the same run and nothing notices. The lost page is real: class Verdict (scripts/run_skill_eval.py:178) and def verdict (:407) both resolve to map/scripts.run_skill_eval/Verdict.md because render.py:405 derives the filename from key.split(':',1)[1] with no collision or case check, and this filesystem is case-insensitive, as is CI's windows-latest. I confirmed the surviving file holds the FUNCTION page; the class is unreachable from the map while the module INDEX.md still links to it. No test in tests/ reads any of the three run reports. Second consequence: the map is platform-dependent, so on a case-sensitive filesystem the same source renders 3636 pages, failing the spec's own determinism falsifier.

payload.question: B1: every rendered page carries a source position, contradicting the settled/human ruling 'nothing committed carries a position' (disposition of BLOCKING critic finding SY1). Either (a) strip the suffix and assign it to a named gate, or (b) amend the ruling and accept SY1's measured churn of ~450 position-bearing lines rewritten per 3-line source edit.
payload.answer: Tommy, verbatim: 'strip the line numbers'. Option (a).
payload.commander_ruling: Done in g0, not deferred. The reviewer's argument for blocking was that map/ is committed at gs, last of eleven, so finding it there means eight gates built on a page format that must change; g0 ships the renderer so g0 fixes it. On what 'the line numbers' means: REMOVE the :<line> component (the cross-page churn SY1 measured), KEEP the bare file path (changes only when the file moves, so it does not churn) and KEEP ', N lines' (an entity's size changes only its own page, which is correct behavior). No new cache is built: .code-map/statements.jsonl already carries per-statement file/line/col and is already gitignored at .gitignore:29, so the rebuildable position store the ruling calls for already exists -- verified by me directly. Falsifier required: a test asserting no rendered page matches a .py:<line> pattern, proven load-bearing by restoring the suffix and watching it go red.
payload.scope_note: B1 and B2 now go to ONE remediation implementer pass rather than two, since the answer arrived before dispatch.

Over the real 3,635-page corpus: 0 entity-page headers carry a .py:<line>, 3522 kept the path, 3522 kept the size (3522 not 3523 because one entity page is the still-lost Verdict page).
payload.b2_fix: render.py:436: npages = sum(1 for _ in out.rglob('*.md')), read off the tree after it is written; the three per-write increments and the nonlocal are gone. Figure moved 3636 -> 3635 against an unchanged on-disk 3635, with the Verdict page still lost, which is the required outcome.
payload.commander_independent_verification: I reproduced BOTH falsifiers in my own hands with a script that asserts each mutation applied before running: baseline 17 passed / 13 subtests; B1 mutated (source line number put back into the header) -> RED on RenderedPageFormatTests::test_no_rendered_page_carries_a_source_line_number; B2 mutated (write-call count restored) -> RED on RenderReportTests::test_render_report_page_count_equals_the_files_on_disk; restored -> 17 passed, working tree byte-identical. Diff is 2 files, 191 insertions. Zero MUTATION PROBE strings left in render.py. map/ still untracked.
payload.crew_corrected_two_errors_in_my_handoff: First, my handoff (repeating the reviewer's B1 text) claimed render.py:306 also emits a position. It does not -- the module index already emitted 'file, N lines' with no line number, so following my instruction literally would have meant editing a compliant line. loc() was the only position emitter. Second, I offered a free choice between 'a set of resolved paths' and 'counting files after the fact'. Only one branch is correct: on a case-insensitive filesystem Verdict.md and verdict.md are two distinct strings and one file, so a set would still have reported 3636 and failed my own acceptance figure. The crew ruled correctly against my wording in both cases and said so.
payload.fixture_design_note: The B2 fixture deliberately collides a class named INDEX with its own module's INDEX.md -- an EXACT-path collision that diverges on every platform -- rather than mimicking the real Verdict/verdict pair, which collides only on a case-insensitive filesystem and would prove nothing on Linux. That is the right call and worth carrying forward: a falsifier whose mechanism is platform-dependent is a check that cannot fail on half the platforms.

Full rebuild at HEAD: 0 of 3535 entity-page headers carry a .py:<line>; 3535/3535 kept the path and ', N lines'. Full suite in a cleared environment 1709 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed. Every constraint held, no regression, and the blast radius of the header format change enumerated by command as zero readers anywhere in scripts/ or tests/. It also confirmed the remediation implementer was RIGHT to overrule my handoff on render.py:306 -- module_index was already compliant.
payload.b3_finding: THE FIX I ACCEPTED RELOCATED THE TAUTOLOGY INSTEAD OF REMOVING IT. render.py:436 now defines pages as sum(1 for _ in out.rglob('*.md')), a count of the tree it describes, so it is tautologically true of that tree and can reveal nothing about it. B2's original finding was 'a page is silently lost, and the count that would reveal it cannot fail'; after the fix the count still cannot fail, having moved from tautological-with-the-writes to tautological-with-the-tree. The lost page is still invisible. Proved by mutation on a byte-exact-restore harness, not by reading: N8 (unlink every second entity page immediately after writing, deleting 25% of the tree) leaves ALL 17 TESTS GREEN; N4 (never write any module INDEX.md, removing 112 pages and the entire navigation layer) leaves ALL 17 GREEN; N5 (write every entity page flat into map/, destroying the documented layout) leaves ALL 17 GREEN. The new test stays green through all three because it computes its expected value with the SAME rglob('*.md') expression as the implementation under test (tests/test_code_map.py:142 against render.py:436), so it guards the counting METHOD and nothing else.
payload.commander_ruling_accept: ACCEPTED IN FULL. I was wrong to accept the tree-count as closing B2, and my own re-verification missed it for the second time at this gate: I reproduced the falsifier the crew built and never asked whether that falsifier could catch anything else. The lesson is specific and goes on the record for the remaining ten gates -- reproducing the mutation a crew designed only proves the crew's own probe works. A cannot-fail check must be attacked with a mutation the test's author did NOT choose, which is exactly what this reviewer did with N4, N5 and N8.
payload.commander_ruling_scope: g0 closes WITHOUT a render.py change, per the reviewer's own two reasons. (1) tests/test_code_map.py:127-131 ships the claim that 'pages has to be a number that can be WRONG' and that 'the count has to come from the tree'. The second clause is true; the first is now false, because coming from the tree is precisely what makes it unable to be wrong. Shipping that docstring inside the gate whose subject is this defect shape is itself the finding, and correcting it is the g0 fix. (2) tc18 as I filed it tells g1 that entity_pages is 'a one-line fix in the same function' -- and the one-line fix matching g0's own precedent is to count the tree again, producing a SECOND tautological field while g1 records the family as closed.
